metadata.title: Národní zpráva z Mezinárodní studie občanské výchovy

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The document reports the ICCS 2009 implementation in the Czech Republic, including a random selection of 150 schools from the national school registry and final use of data from 144 schools (240 classes; 4,630 students). It describes that all present 8th-grade students in selected schools were tested and that teacher and principal questionnaires were collected, with quality control by IEA staff on 10% of schools. The report does not state whether complex survey weights (e.g., student sampling weights) or replicate-weight methods (BRR/jackknife) were applied in the analyses. Given the nature of the publication (national report with primarily descriptive statistics and multilevel modeling described as HLM-based), the manuscript does not provide enough methodological detail to confirm weight usage; therefore weighting is treated as not reported.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This national ICCS report analyzes scale scores derived from ICCS instruments (e.g., Rasch-based scales for knowledge and Likert/scale indices for attitudes) and does not describe any plausible-value (PV) generation or PV-based achievement modeling. Because the dependent variables are not PV-based cognitive achievement scores in the PISA/TIMSS sense, PV handling is not applicable. The report also does not document a missing-data strategy (e.g., listwise/pairwise deletion, multiple imputation), representing a reporting gap for transparency about how incomplete responses were handled.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used ICCS 2009 Czech Republic main study data collected in 2009. Schools were randomly selected from the registry of schools containing 8th-grade students: 150 initial schools plus two replacement schools per initial school; 147 schools consented and data were used from 144 schools at final processing. Within each participating school, all 8th-grade students present on the test day participated (with an option in other countries to sample one class, but in the Czech Republic all classes were used). The report states that the international center required a minimum of 3,000 students and that final data included 4,630 students; it does not specify additional analytic exclusions beyond the final school set.

data.outcome_summary: This ICCS 2009 Czech national report uses ICCS 2009 8th-grade data (4,630 students from 144 schools) to describe and model civic knowledge and civic/political attitudes. Although the report is not an ML study (no ML algorithms are trained), it estimates multilevel regression models (HLM) and simple regressions to explain outcomes. For civic knowledge, the multilevel model explains 83% of between-school variance and 33% of between-student variance; key positive predictors include frequent TV news viewing (+15.1 points), future voting participation (strongest effect), expected education years (+7.5 points per year), and higher parents’ occupational status, while attending basic schools is associated with lower scores (~-37.4 points). For European civic knowledge, explained variance is 52% between schools and 18% between students, with motivation and media exposure again positive and home language Czech strongly positive. For attitudes, democratic values support is positively related to civic knowledge (about 10% explained in simple regression), and planned voting participation is best predicted by civic knowledge and political interest (full model explains ~37%). Methodological caveat: the report does not document missing-data handling or PV-style procedures, and it does not provide ML-specific validation/metrics because no ML models are used.
